Answer: B
Reason: The CT images demonstrate a mosaic attenuation pattern with alternating areas of hyperlucency (reduced attenuation) and normal lung, along with decreased vascularity in the lucent regions, which is characteristic of the small airway disease and air trapping seen in bronchopulmonary dysplasia. Although the option mentions "chest X-rays" and "lower lobes" (while these are axial CT slices showing upper/mid lung involvement), it is the only choice that correctly identifies the specific mosaic pattern associated with BPD pathology.
